chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Musa, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Mubarak, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a drop of wine or an intoxicating Nabeez that dropped into a pot containing much meat and much broth. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Pour out the broth, or feed it to the Ahl Al-Zimma or the dogs; and as for the meat, wash it and eat it.' I said, 'And if blood dropped into it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The blood is consumed by the fire, if Allah wills.' I said, 'So what if wine or Nabeez dropped into dough, or blood?' He said: 'It spoils.' I said, 'Can I sell it to the Jews and Christians and clarify it to them, for they permit drinking it?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' I said, 'And Al-Fuqa' (a type of fermented drink), is it in the same status if a drop of that drops into something?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that I eat it if a drop of that drops into something of my food.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)
key_terms.الْفُقَّاعُ: Al-Fuqa' (a specific type of fermented drink)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on food contaminated by a drop of wine or blood according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the Shia jurisprudence of 'mixing' (ikhtilat) by distinguishing between the impurity of the liquid itself versus the substance it contaminates, ruling that while broth is discarded, solid meat requires only washing. It further highlights the pragmatic application of 'Ahl al-Kitab' (People of the Book) consuming wine, allowing its sale to them, while the Imam expresses personal dislike (karahat) for fermented drinks mixed with food, reflecting the distinction between ritual purity and practical consumption in Ja'fari fiqh.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Musa, from Al Hassan Bin Al Mubarak, from Zakariyya Bin Adam who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about a drop of wine or Nabeez drops into a pot wherein is a lot of meat and a lot of broth. So heasws said: ‘Discard the broth, or feed it to the Ahl Al-Zimma, or the dogs; and the meat, so wash it and eat it’. I said, ‘Supposing there was the drop of blood in it?’ So heasws said: ‘The blood is consumed by the fire, Allahazwj Willing’. I said, ‘So (what about) wine or Nabeez, or a drop of blood drops in the flour dough?’ So heasws said: ‘It spoils’. I said, ‘Can I sell it to the Jews and the Christians and clarify it to them, for they are permitting drinking it?’ Heasws said: ‘And the fermented drink is at that very status, when a drop drops into something from that?’ Heasws said: ‘Iasws dislike that Iasws eat it when a drop drops into something from myasws meal’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Musa from al-Hassan ibn al-Mubarak from Zakariya ibn Adam who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a large cooking pot with a large amount of meat and broth in it and a drop of wine or al-Nabidh is dropped therein. He (the Imam) said, ’It must be thrown away or fed to the taxpayers or dogs. You can wash the meat and eat it.’ I then asked about what happens if one drop of blood is dropped in it. ’The fire, if Allah wills, eats the blood,’ said the Imam. I then asked about if wine or al-Nabidh by a drop is dropped in flour dough or a drop of blood. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is destroyed.’ I then asked if I can sell it to Jews or Christians and tell all about it because they consider drinking it lawful.’ He (the Imam) said, ’Yes, you can do so.’ I then asked about al-Fuqa‘ (beer) if it is like wine, and al-Nabidh when one drop of it is dropped in something. He (the Imam) said, ‘I do not like to eat it if anything thereof is dropped in my food.’”
